# A saint in the business world: lead from the floor

*Reflection · after reading about a businessman who is on the road to sainthood, and after one bad week of trying to lead from the top*

There is a businessman the Church is studying for sainthood, and the thing people remember about him is not a strategy. It is that he knew the names of the men on the floor, their wives' names, which one had a sick kid. He ran a company of thousands and he was most often found standing next to a machine, asking.

I read that and thought about my own week. I had spent it telling. Telling the planners what the tool could do, telling Daniela what the board should decide, telling my professor what I thought the case was really about. I was right in most of it and it landed in none of it.

You rise by going down. I have written that line before and it sounded like piety. This week it sounds like a method. The planner who finally used the assistant was not the one I convinced; it was the one I sat next to for forty minutes while she showed me her spreadsheet and I said almost nothing. She found the use. I found out what she was afraid of, and it was not the machine. It was looking slow in front of her boss.

So the floor is not a humility exercise. It is where the information is. Authority earned there is the only kind that survives my leaving the room, and leaving the room is the whole point of what I build.

What this changes for me this week: in a first meeting, I ask first and I ask longer than is comfortable. I bring one number, not a deck. And when I catch myself explaining, I stop and ask what the other person has already tried.

The discipline is for showing up. The next step is almost always letting go.
